Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Required unless `stop` is true.

Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. - "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

150	### 4.2 workspace 目录结构观察
151	
152	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
153	
154	workspace 是 olmOCR 的「施工现场+仓库」：队列索引、完成标记、锁、Dolma 结果、Markdown 结果全部落在这里。它被设计成**状态的唯一载体**，于是天然获得两个能力：
155	
156	- **断点续跑**：进程崩了再启动，已完成的项会被跳过；
157	- **多机协同**：把 workspace 放在 S3 上，多台机器对着同一个队列抢活干（第 3 单元展开）。
158	
159	理解 workspace 结构，是看懂 olmOCR 全部工程设计的钥匙。
160	
161	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
162	
163	一次完整的本地运行之后，workspace 长这样（带注释）：
164	
165	```
166	localworkspace/
167	├── work_index_list.csv.zstd     # 队列总索引：zstd 压缩的 CSV，每行 = 组哈希 + 该组的 PDF 路径
168	├── done_flags/                  # 完成标记目录：每个完成的工作组一个空文件
169	│   └── done_<group_hash>.flag
170	├── worker_locks/                # 工作组锁目录：防止两个 worker 同时领同一个活
171	│   └── worker_<group_hash>.lock
172	├── results/                     # Dolma 格式输出（面向预训练语料的 JSONL）
173	│   └── output_<group_hash>.jsonl
174	└── markdown/                    # --markdown 时的人类可读输出，保留输入目录结构
175	    └── olmocr-sample.md
176	```
177	
178	生成时序上：前三个（索引、done_flags、worker_locks）在**任务开始前**创建；后两个（results、markdown）由 worker **每完成一组**写入，最后再放一个 done 标记。
179	
180	#### 4.2.3 源码精读
181	
182	- [olmocr/work_queue.py:26-27](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/work_queue.py#L26-L27)：两个目录名常量 `WORKER_LOCKS_DIR = "worker_locks"`、`DONE_FLAGS_DIR = "done_flags"`，本地和 S3 后端共用同一套命名。
183	- [olmocr/work_queue.py:244-252](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/work_queue.py#L244-L252)：`LocalBackend.__init__` 确定索引路径为 `<workspace>/work_index_list.csv.zstd`，并立即 `os.makedirs` 创建 workspace、done_flags、worker_locks 三个目录——所以哪怕什么活都没干，目录骨架也先建好。
184	- [olmocr/work_queue.py:105-111](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/work_queue.py#L105-L111)：`_compute_workgroup_hash` 把一组路径**排序后**逐个喂给 sha1，得到确定性的组哈希——同一组路径无论在谁机器上算，哈希都相同，这是多机去重的基石。
185	- [olmocr/work_queue.py:127-151](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/work_queue.py#L127-L151)：`populate_queue` 先读旧索引做**路径级去重**（已存在的路径不再入队），再把新路径按 `items_per_group` 切组、算哈希，最后把「组哈希 + 各路径」编码成 CSV 行写回 zstd 文件。
186	- [olmocr/pipeline.py:741-759](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L741-L759)：`worker()` 处理完一个工作组后，把若干 Dolma 文档写成 JSONL，先落临时文件再复制到 `<workspace>/results/output_<hash>.jsonl`（S3 workspace 则改为上传）。
187	- [olmocr/pipeline.py:765-794](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L765-L794)：若带 `--markdown`，对每个文档取 `Source-File` 元数据，用 `get_markdown_path` 算出输出路径并写入纯文本。
188	- [olmocr/pipeline.py:654-695](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L654-L695)：`get_markdown_path` 的路径映射规则——本地路径去掉开头的 `/` 变相对路径（保留目录层级），`s3://` 取 bucket 之后的路径，`tarball::内部路径` 特殊拼接；统一清洗掉 `..` 防路径穿越；扩展名换成 `.md`，落到 `<workspace>/markdown/` 之下。这解释了为什么输入 `./olmocr-sample.pdf` 的输出正好是 `markdown/olmocr-sample.md`。
189	- [olmocr/pipeline.py:796-804](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L796-L804)：更新指标后调用 `work_queue.mark_done(work_item)`——即在 done_flags 里放 `done_<hash>.flag`，该组从此被视为完成。

231	### 4.3 pyproject 入口脚本映射
232	
233	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
234	
235	终端里的 `olmocr` 既不是编译出的二进制，也不是 shell 脚本，而是 Python 打包系统的**console script（控制台脚本）**机制：pip 安装包时，读取包元数据中的 `[project.scripts]` 表，在环境的 `bin/` 目录下生成一个极小的可执行包装器，它 import 你指定的函数并调用。所以「`olmocr` 这个命令」的全部秘密就在 `pyproject.toml` 的一行配置里。
236	
237	此外还有一座「同步-异步之桥」：console script 入口必须是普通同步函数，而主流程 `main()` 是 `async def`。`cli_main()` 用 `asyncio.run()` 把两者接起来。
238	
239	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
240	
241	```
242	你在终端敲: olmocr ./localworkspace --markdown --pdfs x.pdf
243	   ↓
244	环境的 bin/olmocr 包装脚本（pip 安装时生成）
245	   ↓ import
246	pyproject.toml [project.scripts] 指向的 olmocr.pipeline:cli_main
247	   ↓
248	cli_main()  ──asyncio.run()──▶  main()   （异步世界：协程、TaskGroup、信号量……）
249	   ↓
250	argparse 解析参数 → 后续所有流程（见 4.1.2）
251	```
252	
253	等价入口：`python -m olmocr.pipeline 参数...`——它依赖 `pipeline.py` 文件末尾的 `if __name__ == "__main__"` 守卫，README 也专门提到了这一点。
254	
255	#### 4.3.3 源码精读
256	
257	- [pyproject.toml:49-50](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/pyproject.toml#L49-L50)：`[project.scripts]` 表声明 `olmocr = "olmocr.pipeline:cli_main"`——命令名 `olmocr`，调用 `olmocr.pipeline` 模块里的 `cli_main` 函数。第 1-2 讲说「olmocr 命令由 scripts 入口注册」，指的就是这两行。
258	- [olmocr/pipeline.py:1526-1528](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1526-L1528)：`cli_main` 只有 3 行——`asyncio.run(main())`。这就是同步命令行世界与异步流水线之间唯一的桥。

288	**参考答案**：不会。`--help` 由 argparse 在 `main()` 开头处理（[olmocr/pipeline.py:1199-1200](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1199-L1200)），两个入口最终都进入同一个 `main()`；唯一可见差别是 usage 行里的程序名（`pipeline.py` vs `olmocr`）。README 的 `--help` 完整输出见 [README.md:431-436](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/README.md#L431-L436)。
289	
290	## 5. 综合实践
291	
292	**任务：走完一次「输入 → workspace → 输出」的完整旅程，并写出可核查的证据链。**
293	
294	1. 准备输入：从 `tests/gnarly_pdfs/` 里挑一个页数少的 PDF（例如 `ambiguous.pdf`），复制到一个带层级的目录，如 `./mypdfs/sub/demo.pdf`——这样能观察 markdown 输出对目录结构的保留。
295	2. 建立队列骨架（无 GPU 也行）：`olmocr ./localworkspace --stats --pdfs mypdfs/sub/demo.pdf`，然后：
296	   - 画出 `localworkspace/` 的目录树并给每一项写一句注释（对照 4.2.2 的图）；
297	   - 运行 4.2.4 的 `decode_work_index.py`，记录组哈希与路径，确认手工重算一致。
298	3. （有条件者）完整转换：`olmocr ./localworkspace --markdown --pdfs mypdfs/sub/demo.pdf`，验证：
299	   - `localworkspace/markdown/mypdfs/sub/demo.md` 存在且目录层级被保留；
300	   - `results/output_<hash>.jsonl` 的哈希与索引中的组哈希一致；
301	   - done_flags 里出现对应 flag。
302	4. 幂等性检验：把第 2 步（或第 3 步）的命令**原样再跑一遍**。预期：`populate_queue` 的去重逻辑（[olmocr/work_queue.py:136-140](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/work_queue.py#L136-L140)）使索引不会新增重复行；完整跑过的组会因 done flag 被跳过，第二次几乎立刻完成。

304	
305	## 6. 本讲小结
306	
307	- `olmocr ./localworkspace --markdown --pdfs x.pdf` 是标准用法：workspace 位置参数 + `--markdown` 开关 + `--pdfs` 输入列表（支持 PDF/图片/txt 清单/S3 glob）。

# 第一次运行：把一个 PDF 转成 Markdown

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 使用 `olmocr` 命令行把一个 PDF 转成 Markdown 文件。
2. 准确说出 workspace（工作目录）里每个产物的作用：`work_index_list.csv.zstd`、`done_flags/`、`worker_locks/`、`results/`、`markdown/`。
3. 说清楚当你在终端敲下 `olmocr` 回车之后，这行命令是如何一步步映射到 `pyproject.toml` 的 `[project.scripts]`、再到 `olmocr/pipeline.py` 的 `cli_main()` 和 `main()` 的——也就是「命令从哪里来」这条链路。
4. 掌握一个没有 GPU 也能观察 workspace 结构的技巧（利用 `--stats` 在 GPU 检查之前短路返回的时序特点）。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲是第一篇「动手跑代码」的讲义，需要以下背景（均在前面两讲建立）：

- **命令行与 Python 环境**：你已经在干净的 conda 环境（Python ≥ 3.11）里用 pip 安装了 `olmocr`（第 1-2 讲），并且系统里装好了 poppler（`pdftoppm` 等命令可用）。
- **轻量安装 vs GPU 安装**：第 1-2 讲我们强调过，`pip install olmocr` 是轻量安装，**不包含 torch / vLLM 等深度学习框架**。本讲的完整转换流程需要推理服务，因此完整跑通有两条路：
  - **本地 GPU**：安装 `pip install "olmocr[gpu]"`，olmOCR 会自动在本机拉起一个 vLLM 服务器；
  - **远程服务器**：用 `--server http://主机:端口/v1` 指向别人托管的推理服务，本机完全不需要 GPU。
- **两个关键概念**：
  - **workspace（工作区）**：olmOCR 不是「原地转换」的工具，它把所有中间状态和结果都写进一个你指定的目录，这个目录就是 workspace。这样设计的好处是**可断点续跑、可多机协同**（第 3 单元会展开）。
  - **同步入口与异步主函数**：Python 的命令行入口必须是普通同步函数，而 olmOCR 的主流程用了 `asyncio` 异步编程（用 `async def` 定义、内部大量并发）。这两者之间需要一座桥，本讲第 4.3 节会看到这座桥。

如果你暂时没有 GPU，完全没问题——本讲的核心实践特意设计成**无 GPU 也能完成大部分**，详见 4.1.4。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 | 本讲关注点 |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | 项目说明书 | Usage Examples 一节的官方命令与结果查看方式 |
| `pyproject.toml` | 包的构建与安装配置 | `[project.scripts]` 如何注册 `olmocr` 命令 |
| `olmocr/pipeline.py` | 批处理流水线主文件（约 1500 行） | `main()` 的参数与时序、`worker()` 如何落盘结果、`get_markdown_path()`、`cli_main()` |
| `olmocr/work_queue.py` | 工作队列抽象（本讲只看骨架） | `LocalBackend` 在 workspace 里创建了哪些目录和文件 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 olmocr 命令行初体验

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

olmOCR 的标准用法是一条命令：指定一个 workspace 目录、一批输入 PDF、以及想要的输出形态。README 给出的第一条命令是：

```bash
# 下载一个示例 PDF（3 页）
curl -o olmocr-sample.pdf https://olmocr.allenai.org/papers/olmocr_3pg_sample.pdf

# 把它转换成 markdown
olmocr ./localworkspace --markdown --pdfs olmocr-sample.pdf
```

这条命令有三个部分：

| 部分 | 类型 | 含义 |
|---|---|---|
| `./localworkspace` | 位置参数（positional） | workspace 路径，所有中间状态和结果都写在这里；也可以是 `s3://` 开头的 S3 路径用于多机协同 |
| `--markdown` | 开关（flag） | 额外把自然文本写成 Markdown 文件，**保留输入 PDF 的目录结构** |
| `--pdfs olmocr-sample.pdf` | 列表参数 | 输入文件；可以跟多个路径、`*.pdf` 通配符、`.txt` 路径清单、S3 glob，PNG/JPEG 图片也行 |

`--pdfs` 不给也合法——那时 olmOCR 会直接读取 workspace 里已有的队列继续干活（断点续跑）。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

当你运行 `olmocr ./localworkspace --markdown --pdfs x.pdf` 后，`main()` 内部大致按这个顺序推进（本讲只建立地图，第 2 单元逐站精读）：

```
解析参数 (parse_known_args)
  ↓
检查 poppler 可用                     ← 轻量安装也装不了它，必须是系统依赖
  ↓
创建 WorkQueue（本地或 S3 后端）       ← workspace 的目录骨架在这里被创建！
  ↓
收集 --pdfs 输入 → 采样估算页数 → populate_queue 写入队列索引
  ↓
[--stats ?] → 打印统计后直接 return   ← 短路点①：不碰 GPU
[--beaker ?] → 提交集群任务后 return  ← 短路点②
  ↓
检查 GPU（仅在需要本地推理时）
  ↓
下载模型（约 30GB）→ 拉起 vLLM 服务 → 等待就绪
  ↓
启动 N 个 worker 协程并发处理队列
  ↓
输出最终指标汇总
```

注意一个**非常有用的时序细节**：workspace 的创建和队列填充发生在 GPU 检查**之前**。这意味着即使你没有任何 GPU，只要运行到 `--stats` 短路点，workspace 里的队列骨架照样会生成——这是本讲无 GPU 实践的理论依据。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

先看参数定义。`main()` 是一个 `async def` 函数，一进来先构建 argparse：

- [olmocr/pipeline.py:1199-1215](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1199-L1215)：定义 `workspace` 位置参数（本地目录或 `s3://` 路径）、`--pdfs` 列表参数，以及默认模型 `allenai/olmOCR-2-7B-1025-FP8`（Hugging Face 上的 olmOCR-2 7B FP8 量化权重）。
- [olmocr/pipeline.py:1226-1228](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1226-L1228)：`--stats` 与 `--markdown` 两个开关参数的定义。`--markdown` 的帮助文本明确说了「preserving the folder structure of the input pdfs」。

再看关键时序：

- [olmocr/pipeline.py:1325-1332](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1325-L1332)：先 `check_poppler_version()`（就是第 1-2 讲 `check.py` 里那个 poppler 检查的复用——没有它连输入 PDF 都读不了）；然后根据 workspace 是否以 `s3://` 开头，选择 `S3Backend` 或 `LocalBackend` 构造 `WorkQueue`。**构造 `LocalBackend` 的那一刻，workspace 目录骨架就被创建了**（下一节展开）。
- [olmocr/pipeline.py:1334-1375](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1334-L1375)：`--pdfs` 收集逻辑——S3 glob 展开、本地文件按扩展名和文件头魔数分类（`%PDF` 开头当 PDF，PNG/JPEG 魔数当图片），`.txt` 则按「每行一个路径」的清单读入。
- [olmocr/pipeline.py:1377-1412](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1377-L1412)：随机抽样最多 100 个 PDF 用 `PdfReader` 数页数，估算平均页数后计算 `items_per_group`（目标每组的页数 ÷ 平均页数），再调用 `work_queue.populate_queue()` 写入队列索引。
- [olmocr/pipeline.py:1414-1425](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1414-L1425)：`--stats` 和 `--beaker` 两个短路点先后 `return`；**直到这之后**才调用 `check_torch_gpu_available()`。这就是「无 GPU 也能跑到 `--stats`」的源码依据。
- [olmocr/pipeline.py:1429-1451](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1429-L1451)：需要本地推理时先 `download_model()`（首次运行会下载约 30GB 权重，需要耐心），然后启动 vLLM 服务并等待就绪。
- [olmocr/pipeline.py:1455-1462](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1455-L1462)：按 `--workers`（默认 20）创建 worker 协程并 `asyncio.gather` 等待全部完成。

README 的官方用法与结果查看方式见 [README.md:264-303](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/README.md#L264-L303)：包括单 PDF、图片、多 PDF 通配符、远程 server 四种形态，以及 `cat localworkspace/markdown/olmocr-sample.md` 查看结果。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：亲手运行 olmOCR 命令，并根据自己有没有 GPU 选择完整或精简路线，观察命令的输出日志。

**路线 A（推荐所有人先做，无需 GPU，轻量安装即可）**：

1. 操作步骤：
   ```bash
   cd <仓库根目录>   # 仓库自带测试 PDF，省去下载
   olmocr ./localworkspace --stats --pdfs tests/gnarly_pdfs/ambiguous.pdf
   ```
2. 需要观察的现象：
   - 终端先打印加载 `--pdfs`、采样估算页数的日志；
   - 随后打印 workspace 统计信息（`print_stats`，见 [olmocr/pipeline.py:1105](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1105)），然后进程正常退出，**全程没有报 GPU 相关错误**；
   - 当前目录多出了 `localworkspace/`。
3. 预期结果：命令成功退出（退出码 0），`localworkspace/` 下已有队列骨架文件（4.2 节实践会解剖它），但**没有** `results/` 和 `markdown/`——因为还没有任何页面被真正转换。
4. 小提示：若提示缺少 `tqdm` 之类的间接依赖，说明你的轻量环境没带上它，`pip install tqdm` 补齐即可。

**路线 B（有 GPU，或已按第 1-2 讲装好 `olmocr[gpu]`）**：

1. 操作步骤（与 README 完全一致）：
   ```bash
   curl -o olmocr-sample.pdf https://olmocr.allenai.org/papers/olmocr_3pg_sample.pdf
   olmocr ./localworkspace --markdown --pdfs olmocr-sample.pdf
   ```
2. 需要观察的现象：下载模型进度 → vLLM 启动日志 → worker 处理日志 → 结尾的 `FINAL METRICS SUMMARY`（含输入/输出 token 数、失败页率、按尝试次数分布的完成页数）。
3. 预期结果：`localworkspace/markdown/olmocr-sample.md` 出现，内容是该 PDF 三页的 Markdown 文本。若显存不足报 `KV cache is larger than available memory`，按日志提示加 `--gpu_memory_utilization 0.80 --max_model_len 16384` 重试。

**路线 C（无 GPU 但想看完整转换结果，待本地验证）**：向托管了 olmOCR 的推理服务商租用 API（README 列出了 Cirrascale、DeepInfra、Parasail 等），用 `--server URL --api_key KEY --workers 1 --max_concurrent_requests 20` 的形式运行。具体命令见 [README.md:336-351](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/README.md#L336-L351)。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `olmocr ./localworkspace --stats --pdfs x.pdf` 在没有 GPU、也没装 torch 的轻量环境里也能正常运行？

**参考答案**：查看 [olmocr/pipeline.py:1414-1425](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1414-L1425)，`--stats` 分支在 `check_torch_gpu_available()` 之前就 `print_stats(args, work_queue)` 并 `return` 了；而它之前的步骤（poppler 检查、WorkQueue 创建、`--pdfs` 收集）只需要 poppler 和 pypdf 这类轻量依赖。所以进程根本走不到需要 torch 的代码。

**练习 2**：README 里「Convert an Image file」的示例是 `olmocr ./localworkspace --markdown --pdfs random_page.png`。图片是怎么被当作 PDF 流水线的输入的？

**参考答案**：输入收集阶段（[olmocr/pipeline.py:1350-1361](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1350-L1361)）会按魔数判断文件类型，PNG/JPEG 会被归入 `pdf_work_paths`（同一个队列）；后续 `olmocr/image_utils.py` 里的 `convert_image_to_pdf_bytes` 会把图片包成单页 PDF 再走统一流程（第 2 单元 u2-l2 精读）。

**练习 3**：不加 `--pdfs` 直接运行 `olmocr ./localworkspace`（GPU 环境）会发生什么？

**参考答案**：`args.pdfs` 为 `None` 时跳过收集与 `populate_queue`（[olmocr/pipeline.py:1334](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1334) 的 `if args.pdfs:` 不成立），接着 `initialize_queue()` 会加载 workspace 中已有的索引、剔除已完成项。如果队列空了（[olmocr/pipeline.py:1442-1444](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1442-L1444)）就打印 "No work to do, exiting" 退出；否则继续处理剩余任务——这就是断点续跑。

### 4.2 workspace 目录结构观察

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

workspace 是 olmOCR 的「施工现场+仓库」：队列索引、完成标记、锁、Dolma 结果、Markdown 结果全部落在这里。它被设计成**状态的唯一载体**，于是天然获得两个能力：

- **断点续跑**：进程崩了再启动，已完成的项会被跳过；
- **多机协同**：把 workspace 放在 S3 上，多台机器对着同一个队列抢活干（第 3 单元展开）。

理解 workspace 结构，是看懂 olmOCR 全部工程设计的钥匙。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

一次完整的本地运行之后，workspace 长这样（带注释）：

```
localworkspace/
├── work_index_list.csv.zstd     # 队列总索引：zstd 压缩的 CSV，每行 = 组哈希 + 该组的 PDF 路径
├── done_flags/                  # 完成标记目录：每个完成的工作组一个空文件
│   └── done_<group_hash>.flag
├── worker_locks/                # 工作组锁目录：防止两个 worker 同时领同一个活
│   └── worker_<group_hash>.lock
```

### 4.3 pyproject 入口脚本映射

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

终端里的 `olmocr` 既不是编译出的二进制，也不是 shell 脚本，而是 Python 打包系统的**console script（控制台脚本）**机制：pip 安装包时，读取包元数据中的 `[project.scripts]` 表，在环境的 `bin/` 目录下生成一个极小的可执行包装器，它 import 你指定的函数并调用。所以「`olmocr` 这个命令」的全部秘密就在 `pyproject.toml` 的一行配置里。

此外还有一座「同步-异步之桥」：console script 入口必须是普通同步函数，而主流程 `main()` 是 `async def`。`cli_main()` 用 `asyncio.run()` 把两者接起来。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```
你在终端敲: olmocr ./localworkspace --markdown --pdfs x.pdf
   ↓
环境的 bin/olmocr 包装脚本（pip 安装时生成）
   ↓ import
pyproject.toml [project.scripts] 指向的 olmocr.pipeline:cli_main
   ↓
cli_main()  ──asyncio.run()──▶  main()   （异步世界：协程、TaskGroup、信号量……）
   ↓
argparse 解析参数 → 后续所有流程（见 4.1.2）
```

等价入口：`python -m olmocr.pipeline 参数...`——它依赖 `pipeline.py` 文件末尾的 `if __name__ == "__main__"` 守卫，README 也专门提到了这一点。

- [olmocr/pipeline.py:1526-1528](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1526-L1528)：`cli_main` 只有 3 行——`asyncio.run(main())`。这就是同步命令行世界与异步流水线之间唯一的桥。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `olmocr ./localworkspace --markdown --pdfs x.pdf` 是标准用法：workspace 位置参数 + `--markdown` 开关 + `--pdfs` 输入列表（支持 PDF/图片/txt 清单/S3 glob）。
- `main()` 的时序要点：**workspace 骨架与队列填充发生在 GPU 检查之前**，`--stats` 在碰 GPU 前短路返回——因此轻量环境也能完成队列搭建与观察。
- workspace 五大产物：`work_index_list.csv.zstd`（zstd 压缩的 CSV 队列索引，每行 = sha1 组哈希 + 路径）、`done_flags/`（完成标记）、`worker_locks/`（并发锁）、`results/`（Dolma JSONL）、`markdown/`（`--markdown` 时按输入目录结构落盘的 `.md`）。
- 组哈希 = 对组内路径**排序后**做 sha1，确定性保证跨机器一致；done flag 只在整组完成落盘后写入，重跑用整文件覆盖保证最终一致。
- `olmocr` 命令来自 `pyproject.toml` 的 `[project.scripts] olmocr = "olmocr.pipeline:cli_main"`；`cli_main` 用 `asyncio.run(main())` 连接同步入口与异步流水线；`python -m olmocr.pipeline` 是等价入口。

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.
